Devareddiyavara, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.

2. The petitioner herein seeking regular bail in Crime No.272/2023 of Murgod Rural Police Station for the offence punishable under Sections 376 and 506 of Indian Penal Code (for short "IPC") which is pending on the file of Hon'ble I Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Saundatti.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Brief facts of the case:
It is the case of the complainant that the petitioner and the victim were loving each other for two and half years.
It is stated that the petitioner on the pretext of marriage said to have committed sexual intercourse on several occasions.
Whenever, the victim insisted the petitioner to marry her, the petitioner one or the other pretext used to postpone the matter.
However, on 08.09.2023 when the victim had been to nature call, the petitioner said to have committed sexual intercourse.

By NC:
2023:KHC-D:13207 then, the victim raised hue and cry.
Consequently, the brother and others went near the place, the victim said to have narrated the incident.

Later,
on 11.09.2023 the complaint came to be registered against the petitioner.
4. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is innocent of alleged offence and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
The victim is aged about 24 years and they were loving each other.
Due to difference of opinion, the petitioner refused to marry her.
Therefore, he was falsely implicated in this case for not having married the victim.

5. Further, it is submitted that even though the allegation made against the petitioner by the victim that the petitioner had committed sexual intercourse on several occasions since two and half years, a case has been registered on 11.09.2023, that itself indicates that the victim consented party and no ingredients in respect of the offence under Section 375 of IPC are not made against the petitioner.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for bail.
Making such submission, the learned counsel for the petitioner prays to allow the petition.
6. Per contra Shri Praveena Y. Devareddiyavara, learned HCGP filed objection and vehemently opposed the bail petition and submitted that the alleged offence is heinous in nature.

The victim has Suresh Maruti Arabhanvi S/O Maruti ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46555274/
2 been subjected to rape on several occasions on pretext of marrying her.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said offence is scar on her reputation and also life.
The overt- act of the petitioner has been established by the investigating officer by filing the charge sheet.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for bail.
Making such submission, the learned HCGP prays to dismiss the petition.
7. Having heard the learned counsel for respective parties and also perused the averments of the charge sheet, admittedly, the victim is aged about 24 years.
Both victim and petitioner were loving each other and they wanted to marry each other.
However, due to difference of opinion between their families, the petitioner NC: 2023:KHC-D:13207 refused to marry her.
As per the averments of the complaint, the petitioner committed sexual intercourse with the victim on several occasions.
Whenever the victim insisted the petitioner to marry her, he used to postpone the matter one or the other pretext and not interested in marring her.
The averments of the complaint and charge sheet make it clear that the ingredients of Section 375 of IPC are not made out against the petitioner.
Therefore, prima facie, I am of the considered opinion that, it is appropriate to grant bail.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.272/2023 of Murgod Rural Police Station for the offence punishable under Sections 376 and 506 of Indian Penal Code (for short "IPC") which is pending on the file of Hon'ble I Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Saundatti on executing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
NC: 2023:KHC-D:13207 (Rupees One lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Trial Court, subject to the following conditions:
a) The petitioner shall not threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses nor hamper the proceedings of the Court.
b) The petitioner shall appear before the Trial Court on all dates of hearing without fail.
In case, if the petitioner violates any of the bail conditions as stated above, the prosecution will be at liberty to seek for cancellation of bail.
